posts.author: Ed Wesly
posts.content_md:
Most Fe EDTA bleach formulae use the sodium form. But I have a bottle of Fe-Ammonium-EDTA. Will the results be identical? I'm thinking it should, since it's just that Fe+ action that we need. Would I have to change the amount of EDTA in the formula based on the difference in molecular weight between sodium and ammonia?

I don't want to order more Fe Na EDTA since it's pushing almost $200/lb.! Of course you can make it for cheaper using the Ferric Sulfate - EDTA trick, but that would still mean ordering more stuff for me. I appreciate any input.

posts.author: jeff-blyth
posts.content_md:
I have never tried that salt . I guess it should work the same. It possibly might cause a bit more contraction from AgBr going into solution. It could give better results to lower the concentration but if you are in a classroom situation Ed I appreciate that time for bleaching is something you don’t have enough of..

Jeff

posts.author: Martin
posts.content_md:
> **Ed Wesly:** Most Fe EDTA bleach formulae use the sodium form. But I have a bottle of Fe-Ammonium-EDTA.

We used it back then, when we were unable to get the Na EDTA. It worked fine (I actually still have a bottle of EDTA bleach, prepared in 1991 – and it still bleaches nicely). The only inconvenience we found was kind of a sludge that formed, which hat to be filtered.
